item.title: A Curious Case of Selenium Manager Usage: What's Behind Chrome 127.0.6533.99?
item.description:
Over the past two years, Selenium has included Selenium Manager, a CLI tool (written in Rust) that provides automatic management of drivers and browsers across all official language bindings (Java, JavaScript, Python, .NET, and Ruby). Its purpose is to simplify the developer experience: if you create a driver object like this:

WebDriver driver = new ChromeDriver();

Selenium Manager takes care of detecting whether Chrome is installed, downloading the required driver, and even provisioning a copy of Chrome for Testing (CfT) if Chrome is not present on the system. This also works for Firefox and Edge, on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
